requirements.canonical: The `override` directive IS overriding the specified attribute for all declarations at all lower scopes that do not also declare the specified attribute.
requirements.original: The override directive overrides the specified attribute for all declarations at all lower scopes that do not also declare the specified attribute.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence seems to conflict with 27.1.2.0-s022, which states that the override directive overwrites attribute definitions of lower scopes. Example 6 (MyRecordD.fieldC keeps RuleC against the group's override RuleA) suggests that a lower declaration with its own override directive is kept. Reading 1 is chosen.
readings: The `override` directive IS overriding the specified attribute for all lower-scope declarations, except those lower-scope declarations that declare the same attribute with an `override` directive themselves.
The `override` directive IS overriding the specified attribute only for lower-scope declarations that do not declare the specified attribute at all.

requirements.subject: ent:override-directive
requirements.condition: the override directive is applied to a type reference
requirements.canonical: If the `override` directive is applied to a type reference, the `override` directive IS NOT affecting the attributes of the original referenced type.
requirements.original: If the override directive is applied to a type reference, it does not affect the attributes of the original referenced type.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.canonical: An attribute definition directly attached to a field or element of a structured type IS overriding the corresponding attribute of the structured type for the identified field or element.
requirements.original: An attribute definition directly attached to a field or element of a structured type overrides the corresponding attribute of the structured type, as regards the identified field or element.

requirements.subject: ent:override-directive
requirements.canonical: An attribute with the `override` directive applied to a synonym type IS overriding the attributes of all fields or elements of the synonym type, unless the synonym type definition contains an explicit attribute definition for the field or element.
requirements.original: Override attribute applied to a synonym type (clause 6.4) overrides attributes of all fields or elements of the synonym type unless the synonym type definition contains an explicit attribute definition for the field or element.

ambiguity.issue: 'Override attribute' is used for an attribute carrying the override directive.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: A variant attribute IS always related to an encode attribute.
requirements.original: A variant attribute is always related to an encode attribute.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: A variant attribute MAY change without changing the related encode attribute.
requirements.original: Whereas a variant of an encoding may change,

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: An encode attribute SHALL NOT change without overwriting all current variant attributes.
requirements.original: an encoding shall not change without overwriting all current variant attributes.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether the user is required to overwrite the variant attributes explicitly, or whether a change of the encoding implicitly deactivates the current variant attributes (as stated in 27.1.2.1-s007). Reading 1 is chosen because of the list that follows.
readings: When an encode attribute changes, all current variant attributes ARE overwritten (made inactive) implicitly.
An encode attribute SHALL NOT be changed unless all current variant attributes are explicitly overwritten in the same `with` statement.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: The core language standard IS defining the default overwriting rules for variant attributes.
requirements.original: The present document defines the default rules for variant attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:extension-package
requirements.canonical: An extension package of TTCN-3, for example a language mapping, MAY define its own overwriting rules for variant attributes.
requirements.original: Extension packages of TTCN-3, for example specifying language mappings, may define their own overwriting rules for variant attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: A variant attribute IS overwriting a current variant attribute according to the overwriting rules defined in clause 27.1.2.
requirements.original: a variant attribute overwrites a current variant attribute according to the rules defined in clause 27.1.2;

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: An encode attribute that overwrites a current encode attribute according to the rules of clause 27.1.2 IS also overwriting the corresponding current variant attribute.
requirements.original: an encoding attribute, which overwrites a current encoding attribute according to the rules defined in clause 27.1.2, also overwrites a corresponding current variant attribute

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: When an encode attribute overwrites a current encode attribute and no new variant attribute is provided, the corresponding current variant attribute IS inactive.
requirements.original: i.e. no new variant attribute is provided, but the current variant attribute becomes inactive;

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: An encode attribute that changes a current encode attribute of an imported language element according to the rules of clause 27.1.3 IS also changing the corresponding current variant attribute.
requirements.original: an encoding attribute, which changes a current encoding attribute of an imported language element according to the rules defined in clause 27.1.3, also changes a corresponding current variant attribute

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: When an encode attribute changes the current encode attribute of an imported language element and no new variant attribute is provided, the corresponding current variant attribute IS inactive.
requirements.original: i.e. no new variant attribute is provided, but the current variant attribute becomes inactive.

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: An encode attribute of a higher scope that is explicitly listed again in the lower scope and is not overwritten IS retaining all variant attributes related to it.
requirements.original: Explicitly listed encode attributes that occur on the higher scope and are not overwritten will retain all variants related to them.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether 'explicitly listed' refers to the listing in the higher scope or to re-listing in the lower scope. The example (Int2 keeps the CodecA variant because CodecA is listed again, CodecB is discarded) supports reading 1.
readings: An encode attribute of a higher scope that is explicitly listed again in the lower scope IS retaining all variant attributes related to it.
An encode attribute that is explicitly listed in a higher scope and not overwritten in the lower scope IS retaining all variant attributes related to it.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: A variant attribute related to an encoding IS overwriting only the variant attributes related to the same encoding.
requirements.original: An encoding related variant will overwrite only variants related to the same encoding.

requirements.subject: ent:language-element
requirements.canonical: An imported language element IS imported together with its attributes.
requirements.original: In general, a language element is imported together with its attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: The attributes of an imported language element MAY be changed by a `with` statement attached to the `import` statement.
requirements.original: For such cases it is allowed to change attributes on the import statement.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: When resolving attributes, the `import` statement IS acting as an additional higher scope unit on top of the imported module.
requirements.original: When resolving the attributes, the import statement works as an additional higher scope unit on the top of the imported module.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An attribute set in the `import` statement IS valid only within the importing module.
requirements.original: Attributes set in the import statement are valid only within the importing module.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An `import` statement IS located inside an importing module and possibly inside a group.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: The import statement occurs inside an importing module and sometimes inside a group.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.canonical: The attributes of the importing module and of an enclosing group of an `import` statement ARE applying to the imported module too.
requirements.original: Because of the scope rules, attributes of these scope units apply to the imported module too.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.condition: the imported definition has its own with statement
requirements.canonical: If a `with` statement is added to an import of a definition that has its own `with` statement, the attributes of that definition ARE overwriting the attributes added to the `import` statement.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: If a with statement is added to an import of a definition where a local definition also has a with statement, the local definition's attributes overwrite the attributes added to the import statement in the normal way.

ambiguity.issue: 'local definition' denotes the definition in the imported module, not a local definition in the sense of a definition inside a behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:override-directive
requirements.canonical: To change the attributes of an imported definition that has its own `with` statement via the `import` statement, the `override` directive SHALL be used.
requirements.original: Thus, if the attributes of a local definition is to be changed via the import statement, the override directive needs to be used.

requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.canonical: The `with` statement IS used to associate attributes to TTCN-3 language elements and to sets of language elements.
requirements.original: The with statement is used to associate attributes to TTCN-3 language elements (and sets thereof).

requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.canonical: The `with` statement has the syntax `with "{" { ( encode | variant | display | extension | optional ) [ override | @local ] [ "(" DefinitionRef | FieldReference | AllRef ")" ] [ ( FreeText | ( "{" FreeText { "," FreeText } "}" ) ) "." ] FreeText [ ";" ] } "}"`.
requirements.original:
with "{" 
   { ( encode | variant | display | extension | optional )
    [ override | @local ]
    ["(" DefinitionRef | FieldReference | AllRef ")"] 
    [ ( FreeText | ("{" FreeText { "," FreeText } "}") ) "." ] FreeText [";"] }
  "}"

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.canonical: There ARE five kinds of attributes that can be associated with a language element: display, encode, variant, extension and optional.
requirements.original: There are five kinds of attributes that can be associated to language elements:

requirements.subject: ent:display-attribute
requirements.canonical: The `display` attribute IS allowing the specification of display attributes related to specific presentation formats.
requirements.original: a) display: allows the specification of display attributes related to specific presentation formats;

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: The `encode` attribute IS allowing references to specific encoding rules.
requirements.original: b) encode: allows references to specific encoding rules;

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: The `variant` attribute IS allowing references to specific encoding variants.
requirements.original: c) variant: allows references to specific encoding variants;

requirements.subject: ent:extension-attribute
requirements.canonical: The `extension` attribute IS allowing the specification of user-defined attributes.
requirements.original: d) extension: allows the specification of user-defined attributes;

requirements.subject: ent:optional-attribute
requirements.canonical: The `optional` attribute IS allowing the implicit setting of optional fields of records and sets to `omit`.
requirements.original: e) optional: allows the implicit setting of optional fields in records and sets to omit.

requirements.subject: ent:free-text
requirements.canonical: The argument of an attribute in a `with` statement (the actual attribute) IS a free text string.
requirements.original: The syntax for the argument of the with statement (i.e. the actual attributes) is defined as a free text string.

requirements.subject: ent:definition-ref
requirements.canonical: A DefinitionRef or FieldReference in a `with` statement IS identifying a definition or field, respectively, within the module, group or definition to which the `with` statement is associated.
requirements.original: _DefinitionRef and FieldReference identify a definition or field respectively which is within the module, group or_ definition to which the with statement is associated.

requirements.subject: ent:all-ref
requirements.canonical: An AllRef MAY be used to apply attributes to multiple language elements defined within the scope to which the `with` statement is associated.
requirements.original: _AllRef can be used to apply attributes to multiple language elements defined within the scope to which the with_ statement is associated.

requirements.subject: ent:all-ref
requirements.canonical: An AllRef IS selecting all language elements, or all language elements of a certain kind, defined in a given scope.
requirements.original: AllRef provides a flexible mechanism to select all language elements or all language elements of a certain kind defined in a given scope.

requirements.subject: ent:except-clause
requirements.canonical: An individual language element that is not affected by an attribute MAY be excluded from a set of language elements selected by an AllRef by means of the except clause.
requirements.original: Individual language elements that are not affected by an attribute can be excluded from a set of selected language elements in the except clause.

requirements.subject: ent:definition-ref
requirements.canonical: A DefinitionRef or FieldReference in a `with` statement SHALL refer to a definition or field, respectively, which is within the module, group or definition to which the `with` statement is associated.
requirements.original: a) _DefinitionRef and FieldReference shall refer to a definition or field respectively which is within the module,_ group or definition to which the with statement is associated.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.condition: multiple attributes of the same kind are allowed
requirements.canonical: If multiple attributes of the same kind are allowed in a `with` statement, all of them SHALL be without an additional modifier (`override`, `@local`) or all of them SHALL have the same modifier.
requirements.original: b) In case multiple attributes of the same type are allowed, all of them shall be without an additional modifier (override, @local) or the modifier shall be the same for all attributes.

ambiguity.issue: 'type' is used for the kind of attribute (encode, variant, ...), which can be confused with TTCN-3 types.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: Dot notation in the FreeText part of an attribute SHALL NOT be used in attributes other than variant attributes.
requirements.original: c) Dot notation in the FreeText part is allowed for variant attributes only.

requirements.subject: ent:display-attribute
requirements.canonical: A display attribute IS allowing the specification of display attributes related to specific presentation formats.
requirements.original: Display attributes allow the specification of display attributes related to specific presentation formats.

requirements.subject: ent:display-attribute
requirements.canonical: The display attribute IS introduced by the keyword `display`.
requirements.original: display

requirements.subject: ent:language-element
requirements.canonical: Every TTCN-3 language element MAY have display attributes that specify how the language element is displayed, e.g. in a tabular format.
requirements.original: All TTCN-3 language elements can have display attributes to specify how particular language elements shall be displayed in, for example, a tabular format.

requirements.subject: ent:display-attribute
requirements.canonical: Special attribute strings related to the display attributes for the graphical presentation format ARE defined in ETSI ES 201 873-3.
requirements.original: Special attribute strings related to the display attributes for the graphical presentation format can be found in ETSI ES 201 873-3 [i.2].

requirements.subject: ent:display-attribute
requirements.canonical: A user MAY define other display attributes.
requirements.original: Other display attributes may be defined by the user.

requirements.subject: ent:user-defined-attribute
requirements.canonical: Because user-defined attributes are not standardized, the interpretation of a user-defined attribute MAY differ between tools or MAY not be supported.
requirements.original: NOTE: Because user-defined attributes are not standardized, the interpretation of these attributes may differ between tools or even may not be supported.

requirements.subject: ent:display-attribute
requirements.canonical: At most one display attribute SHALL be applied to each definition, each individual field reference or each language element to which a `with` statement is associated.
requirements.original: a) At most one display attribute shall be applied to each definition, each individual field reference or language element to which a with statement is associated.

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: General or particular encoding rules MAY be specified by using encode and variant attributes.
requirements.original: In TTCN-3, general or particular encoding rules can be specified by using encode and variant attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: An encode attribute IS allowing references to specific encoding rules.
requirements.original: Encoding attributes allow references to specific encoding rules.

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: The encode attribute IS introduced by the keyword `encode`.
requirements.original: encode

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-rule
requirements.canonical: An encoding rule IS defining how a value, template, etc. is encoded and transmitted over a communication port and how received signals are decoded.
requirements.original: Encoding rules define how a particular value, template, etc. shall be encoded and transmitted over a communication port and how received signals shall be decoded.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-language
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language IS NOT having a default encoding mechanism.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 does not have a default encoding mechanism.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-rule
requirements.canonical: Encoding rules and encoding directives ARE defined in some manner external to TTCN-3.
requirements.original: This means that encoding rules or encoding directives are defined in some external manner to TTCN-3.

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: The encode attribute IS associating a referenced encoding rule or encoding directive with a TTCN-3 definition.
requirements.original: The encode attribute allows the association of some referenced encoding rule or encoding directive to be made to a TTCN-3 definition.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-rule
requirements.canonical: The manner in which the actual encoding rules are defined (e.g. prose, functions) IS outside the scope of the core language standard.
requirements.original: The manner in which the actual encoding rules are defined (e.g. prose, functions, etc.) is outside the scope of the present document.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: no specific encoding rules are referenced
requirements.canonical: If no specific encoding rules are referenced, the encoding SHALL be a matter for the individual implementation.
requirements.original: If no specific rules are referenced then encoding shall be a matter for individual implementation.

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: Encoding attributes ARE in most cases used in a hierarchical manner.
requirements.original: In most cases encoding attributes will be used in a hierarchical manner.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-hierarchy
requirements.canonical: In the encoding hierarchy the top level IS the entire module, the next level IS a group and the lowest level IS an individual type or definition.
requirements.original: The top-level is the entire module, the next level is a group and the lowest is an individual type or definition:

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: An encode attribute associated with a module IS applying to all types defined in the module, including the built-in TTCN-3 types.
requirements.original: a) module: encoding applies to all types defined in the module, including TTCN-3 types (built-in types);

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear how a module-level encode attribute can apply to built-in types, which are not defined in the module; read as: built-in types used in the module are encoded with the module rule.
readings: An encode attribute associated with a module IS applying to all types defined in the module and to built-in types used within the module.
An encode attribute associated with a module IS applying only to types defined in the module, and built-in types are included only where they are referenced by such definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: An encode attribute associated with a group IS applying to the user-defined type definitions of the group.
requirements.original: b) group: encoding applies to a group of user-defined type definitions;

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: An encode attribute associated with a type or definition IS applying to that single user-defined type or definition.
requirements.original: c) type or definition: encoding applies to a single user-defined type or definition;

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: An encode attribute associated with a field IS applying to that field of a record type, set type or template.
requirements.original: d) field: encoding applies to a field in a record or set type or template.

requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement MAY contain more than one encode attribute.
requirements.original: The with statement may contain more than one encode attribute.

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.condition: the with statement contains more than one encode attribute
requirements.canonical: If a `with` statement contains more than one encode attribute, multiple encodings ARE supported in the context where the attribute is used.
requirements.original: In this case, multiple encodings are supported in the context where the attribute is used.

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.canonical: The encoding used in encoding and decoding operations MAY be selected dynamically by the `setencode` operation, by a parameter of the predefined codec functions, or inside the codec implementation.
requirements.original: The encoding used in the encoding and decoding operations can be selected dynamically by using the setencode operation (clause C.5), as a parameter of predefined codec functions (clause C.5) or inside the codec implementation.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-rule
requirements.canonical: General or particular encoding rules CAN be specified by `encode` and `variant` attributes.
requirements.original: In TTCN-3, general or particular encoding rules can be specified by using encode and variant attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: A `variant` attribute IS a reference to a specific encoding variant.
requirements.original: Variant attributes allow references to specific encoding variants.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: A variant attribute IS denoted by the keyword `variant` in a with statement.
requirements.original: variant

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: a refinement, not a replacement, of the current encoding scheme is to be specified
requirements.canonical: A `variant` attribute SHALL be used to specify a refinement of the currently specified encoding scheme instead of its replacement.
requirements.original: To specify a refinement of the currently specified encoding scheme instead of its replacement, the variant attribute shall be used.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: A `variant` attribute IS closely related to `encode` attributes and therefore differs from other attributes.
requirements.original: The variant attributes are different from other attributes, because they are closely related to encode attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: Additional overwriting rules defined in clause 27.1.2.1 apply to `variant` attributes.
requirements.original: Therefore, for variant attributes, additional overwriting rules apply (see clause 27.1.2.1).

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: The set of predefined (standardized) variant attributes for simple basic types IS given in list items a) to e) of clause 27.5 ("8 bit" ... "IEEE754 extended double").
requirements.original: The following strings are the predefined (standardized) variant attributes for simple basic types (see clause E.2.1):

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "8 bit" or "unsigned 8 bit" applied to an integer or enumerated type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "8 bit" or "unsigned 8 bit" is applied to an integer or enumerated type, the integer value or the integer numbers associated with the enumerated values SHALL be handled as represented on 8 bits (single byte) within the system.
requirements.original: a) "8 bit" and "unsigned 8 bit" mean, when applied to integer and enumerated types, that the integer value or the integer numbers associated with enumerated values shall be handled as it was represented on 8-bits (single byte) within the system.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "16 bit" or "unsigned 16 bit" applied to an integer or enumerated type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "16 bit" or "unsigned 16 bit" is applied to an integer or enumerated type, the integer value or the integer numbers associated with the enumerated values SHALL be handled as represented on 16 bits (two bytes) within the system.
requirements.original: b) "16 bit" and "unsigned 16 bit" mean, when applied to integer and enumerated types, that the integer value or the integer numbers associated with enumerated values shall be handled as it was represented on 16-bits (two bytes) within the system.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "32 bit" or "unsigned 32 bit" applied to an integer or enumerated type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "32 bit" or "unsigned 32 bit" is applied to an integer or enumerated type, the integer value or the integer numbers associated with the enumerated values SHALL be handled as represented on 32 bits (four bytes) within the system.
requirements.original: c) "32 bit" and "unsigned 32 bit" mean, when applied to integer and enumerated types, that the integer value or the integer numbers associated with enumerated values shall be handled as it was represented on 32-bits (four bytes) within the system.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "64 bit" or "unsigned 64 bit" applied to an integer or enumerated type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "64 bit" or "unsigned 64 bit" is applied to an integer or enumerated type, the integer value or the integer numbers associated with the enumerated values SHALL be handled as represented on 64 bits (eight bytes) within the system.
requirements.original: d) "64 bit" and "unsigned 64 bit" mean, when applied to integer and enumerated types, that the integer value or the integer numbers associated with enumerated values shall be handled as it was represented on 64-bits (eight bytes) within the system.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: an IEEE754 variant is applied to a float type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "IEEE754 float", "IEEE754 double", "IEEE754 extended float" or "IEEE754 extended double" is applied to a float type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to IEEE 754.
requirements.original: e) "IEEE754 float","IEEE754 double", "IEEE754 extended float" and "IEEE754 extended double" mean, when applied to a float type, that the value shall be encoded and decoded according to the standard IEEE 754 [6] (see annex E).

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: The set of predefined (standardized) variant attributes for charstring and universal charstring types IS given in list items a) to h) following this sentence ("UTF-8" ... "8 bit").
requirements.original: The following strings are the predefined (standardized) variant attributes for charstring and `universal` charstring (see clause E.2.2):

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "UTF-8" applied to a universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "UTF-8" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-8 as defined in clause 10.1 of ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: a) "UTF-8" means, when applied to the universal charstring type, that the value shall be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-8 as defined in clause 10.1 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "UTF-16" applied to a universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "UTF-16" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-16 as defined in clause 10.4 of ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: b) "UTF-16" means, when applied to the universal charstring type, that the value shall be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-16 as defined in clause 10.4 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "UTF-16LE" applied to a universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "UTF-16LE" is applied to a universal charstring type, each character of the value SHALL be individually encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-16LE as defined in clause 10.3 of ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: c) "UTF-16LE" means, when applied to the universal charstring type, that each character of the value shall be individually encoded and decoded according to the UCS Encoding scheme UTF-16LE as defined in clause 10.3 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].

ambiguity.issue: Only "UTF-16LE" (and the charstring "8 bit") prescribes individual encoding of each character; all other UTF variants encode "the value". It is unclear whether the difference is intended. Chose the literal wording.
readings: When the variant attribute "UTF-16LE" is applied to a universal charstring type, each character of the value SHALL be individually encoded and decoded according to UTF-16LE.
When the variant attribute "UTF-16LE" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value as a whole SHALL be encoded and decoded according to UTF-16LE, like the other UTF variants.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "UTF-16BE" applied to a universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "UTF-16BE" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-16BE as defined in clause 10.2 of ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: d) "UTF-16BE" means, when applied to the universal charstring type, that the value shall be encoded and decoded according to the UCS Encoding scheme UTF-16BE as defined in clause 10.2 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "UTF-32" applied to a universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "UTF-32" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-32 as defined in clause 10.7 of ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: e) "UTF-32" means, when applied to the universal charstring type, that the value shall be encoded and decoded according to the UCS Encoding scheme UTF-32 as defined in clause 10.7 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "UTF-32LE" applied to a universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "UTF-32LE" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-32LE as defined in clause 10.6 of ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: f) "UTF-32LE" means, when applied to the universal charstring type, that the value shall be encoded and decoded according to the UCS Encoding scheme UTF-32LE as defined in clause 10.6 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "UTF-32BE" applied to a universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "UTF-32BE" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-32BE as defined in clause 10.5 of ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: g) "UTF-32BE" means, when applied to the universal charstring type, that the value shall be encoded and decoded according to the UCS Encoding scheme UTF-32BE as defined in clause 10.5 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "8 bit" applied to a charstring or universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "8 bit" is applied to a charstring or universal charstring type, each character of the value SHALL be individually encoded and decoded according to the 8-bit coded representation specified in ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: h) "8 bit" means, when applied to charstring and universal charstring types, that each character of the value shall be individually encoded and decoded according to the coded representation as specified in ISO/IEC 10646 [2] (an 8-bit coding).

requirements.subject: ent:ucs-encoding-scheme
requirements.canonical: A UCS encoding scheme permits an optional signature (byte order mark, BOM) to be present in encoded character strings.
requirements.original: NOTE: The UCS Encoding schemes allow an optional signature (also known as Byte Order Mark, BOM) to be present in encoded character strings.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: A UCS encoding scheme variant attribute IS NOT specifying whether signatures (BOM) are present in the encoded value; the presence of signatures is an option of the encoder.
requirements.original: The above UCS encoding scheme variant attributes does not specify, if signatures are present in the encoded values or not, this is an option for the encoder.

ambiguity.issue: "does not specify, if signatures are present" uses the plural verb mismatch and "signatures" for BOM; meaning is clear.

requirements.subject: ent:decoder
requirements.canonical: A decoder SHOULD be able to process signatures (BOM) in the decoding process.
requirements.original: It is expected that decoders are able to process signatures in the decoding process.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: The set of predefined (standardized) variant attributes for structured types IS given in list item a) following this sentence ("IDL:fixed FORMAL/01-12-01 v.2.6").
requirements.original: The following strings are the predefined (standardized) variant attributes for structured types (see clause E.2.2.4):

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "IDL:fixed FORMAL/01-12-01 v.2.6" applied to a record type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "IDL:fixed FORMAL/01-12-01 v.2.6" is applied to a record type, the value SHALL be handled as an IDL fixed point decimal value.
requirements.original: a) "IDL:fixed FORMAL/01-12-01 v.2.6" means, when applied to a record type, that the value shall be handled as an IDL fixed point decimal value (see annex E).

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: A predefined variant attribute MAY be used in combination with a more general encode attribute specified at a higher level.
requirements.original: These variant attributes can be used in combination with the more general encode attributes specified at a higher level.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: UTF-8 variant on a universal charstring inside a module with global encode "BER:1997"
requirements.canonical: When a universal charstring has the variant attribute "UTF-8" within a module that has the global encode attribute "BER:1997", each character of the string value IS first encoded following the UTF-8 rules and the resulting UTF-8 value IS then encoded following the BER rules.
requirements.original: For example a universal charstring specified with the variant attribute "UTF-8" within a module which itself has a global encoding attribute "BER:1997" (see clause 12.2 of ETSI ES 201 873-7 [i.5]) will cause each character of the values within the string to first be encoded following the UTF-8 rules and then this UTF-8 value will be encoded following the more global BER rules.

requirements.subject: ent:invalid-encoding-rule
requirements.condition: invalid encoding rules are to be specified
requirements.canonical: An invalid encoding rule SHALL be specified in a referenceable source external to the module in the same way as valid encoding rules are referenced.
requirements.original: If it is desired to specify invalid encoding rules then these shall be specified in a referenceable source external to the module in the same way that valid encoding rules are referenced.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: multiple encodings (clause 27.4) are used
requirements.canonical: If multiple encodings are used, the value of a variant attribute SHALL be composed of two parts separated by a dot.
requirements.original: If multiple encodings (see clause 27.4) are used, the variant attribute value shall be composed of two parts separated by a dot.

ambiguity.issue: "If multiple encodings are used" does not say where they are used. Chose: multiple encode attributes are associated with the element that the variant applies to.
readings: If multiple encode attributes are associated with the element a variant attribute applies to, the value of that variant attribute SHALL be composed of two parts separated by a dot.
If multiple encodings are used anywhere in the module, the value of every variant attribute SHALL be composed of two parts separated by a dot.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-related-variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: A variant attribute whose value is composed of an encoding reference and a variant value separated by a dot IS called an encoding related variant attribute.
requirements.original: Such variant attributes are called encoding related variant attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-related-variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: The first part (before the dot) of an encoding related variant attribute IS the specification of the encodings the variant is related to.
requirements.original: The first part of the attribute specifies the encodings the variant is related to.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-related-variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant related to a single encoding
requirements.canonical: When the variant is related to a single encode attribute, the first part of an encoding related variant attribute IS a simple string.
requirements.original: There are two possible notations: either a simple string when the variant is related to a single encode attribute or a comma separated list of strings enclosed in curly brackets if the variant is related to multiple encodings.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-related-variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant related to multiple encodings
requirements.canonical: When the variant is related to multiple encodings, the first part of an encoding related variant attribute IS a comma separated list of strings enclosed in curly brackets.
requirements.original: There are two possible notations: either a simple string when the variant is related to a single encode attribute or a comma separated list of strings enclosed in curly brackets if the variant is related to multiple encodings.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-related-variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: The second part (following the dot) of an encoding related variant attribute IS a simple string that specifies the variant value.
requirements.original: The second part of the attribute (following the dot symbol) is a simple string that specifies the variant value.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-related-variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: An encoding related variant attribute IS valid only when the related encoding is selected.
requirements.original: The encoding related attributes are valid only when the related encoding is selected.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: multiple encodings are used
requirements.canonical: If multiple encodings are used, a variant attribute SHALL NOT be defined without an encoding reference.
requirements.original: It is not allowed to define variant attributes with no encoding reference if multiple encodings are used.

requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.canonical: A with statement MAY contain any number of variant attributes.
requirements.original: The with statement can contain any number of variant attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-related-variant-attribute
requirements.condition: dot notation is used in the variant attribute value
requirements.canonical: When dot notation is used in the variant attribute value for an element, the strings preceding the dot SHALL resolve into one of the encode attribute values associated with the same element.
requirements.original: a) When dot notation is used in the variant attribute value for an element, the strings preceding the dot symbol shall resolve into one of the encode attribute values associated with the same element.

requirements.subject: ent:extension-attribute
requirements.canonical: An extension attribute CAN be used for proprietary extensions to TTCN-3.
requirements.original: Extension attributes can be used for proprietary extensions to TTCN-3.

requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.canonical: A with statement MAY contain any number of extension attributes.
requirements.original: The with statement may contain any number of extension attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:extension-attribute
requirements.canonical: An extension attribute IS denoted by the keyword `extension` in a with statement.
requirements.original: extension

requirements.subject: ent:extension-attribute
requirements.canonical: An extension attribute MAY be specified by the user for any TTCN-3 language element.
requirements.original: All TTCN-3 language elements can have extension attributes specified by the user.

requirements.subject: ent:extension-attribute
requirements.canonical: The interpretation of a user-defined (extension) attribute IS not standardized and may differ between tools of different vendors or not be supported at all.
requirements.original: NOTE: Because user-defined attributes are not standardized the interpretation of these attributes between tools supplied by different vendors may differ or even not be supported.

ambiguity.issue: "user-defined attributes" is used for what the clause calls extension attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-attribute
requirements.canonical: An optional attribute IS used to indicate that the optional fields of constants, module parameters, templates, variables and template variables of record and set types are implicitly set to `omit`.
requirements.original: The optional attribute can be used to indicate that optional fields of constants, module parameters, templates, variables and template variables of record and set types are implicitly set to omit.

ambiguity.issue: "can be used to indicate ... implicitly set to omit" ignores that the "explicit omit" value of the same attribute leaves fields undefined. Chose: the attribute controls whether optional fields are implicitly set to omit.
readings: An optional attribute IS used to control whether the optional fields of record and set type definitions are implicitly set to `omit`.
An optional attribute always causes the optional fields of record and set type definitions to be implicitly set to `omit`.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-attribute
requirements.canonical: An optional attribute IS denoted by the keyword `optional` in a with statement.
requirements.original: optional

requirements.subject: ent:optional-attribute
requirements.canonical: An optional attribute MAY be associated with a constant, module parameter, template, variable or template variable.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 constants, module parameters, templates, variables and template variables can have an optional attribute.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-attribute
requirements.canonical: An optional attribute MAY be associated with a module, group, function, altstep, testcase, module control function or component type definition.
requirements.original: Also, TTCN-3 language elements that contain such definitions, i.e. module, group, function, altstep, test case, control, and component type definitions can have an optional attribute.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-attribute
requirements.condition: optional attribute associated with a function, altstep, testcase, control or component type definition
requirements.canonical: When an optional attribute is associated with a function, altstep, testcase, module control function or component type definition, it SHALL have effect on all constants, module parameters, templates, variables and template variables declared within that definition.
requirements.original: When an optional attribute is associated to a function, altstep, test case, control or component type definitions, it shall have effect on all the constants, module parameters, templates, variables and template variables declared within these definitions and not on the enframing definition itself.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-attribute
requirements.condition: optional attribute associated with a function, altstep, testcase, control or component type definition
requirements.canonical: When an optional attribute is associated with a function, altstep, testcase, module control function or component type definition, it SHALL NOT have effect on the enframing definition itself.
requirements.original: When an optional attribute is associated to a function, altstep, test case, control or component type definitions, it shall have effect on all the constants, module parameters, templates, variables and template variables declared within these definitions and not on the enframing definition itself.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-attribute
requirements.condition: no optional attribute value specified directly or inherited
requirements.canonical: When no value of the optional attribute is specified for a definition, either directly or inherited from the surrounding scope, the optional attribute of that definition IS implicitly "explicit omit".
requirements.original: When no value of the optional attribute is explicitly specified for a definition (either directly or inherited from the surrounding scope), the value of the optional attribute is implicitly set to "explicit omit" for that definition.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-attribute
requirements.canonical: The predefined (standardized) optional attribute values IS one of "implicit omit" and "explicit omit".
requirements.original: The following strings are the predefined (standardized) optional attributes:

requirements.subject: ent:implicit-omit
requirements.canonical: With the optional attribute "implicit omit", every optional field that has no assigned value definition in the statement on which the attribute operates IS set to `omit`.
requirements.original: a) "implicit omit" means that all optional fields, that have no assigned value definition in the statement on which the attribute operates, are set to omit.

requirements.subject: ent:implicit-omit
requirements.canonical: The "implicit omit" rule IS applied recursively to the optional fields of the entity and to the subfields of its mandatory fields.
requirements.original: This applies recursively to the optional fields of the entity and to subfields of the mandatory fields.

requirements.subject: ent:explicit-omit
requirements.canonical: With the optional attribute "explicit omit", every optional field that has no assigned value definition in the statement on which the attribute operates IS left undefined.
requirements.original: b) "explicit omit" means that all optional fields, that have no assigned value definition in the statement on which the attribute operates, are left undefined.

requirements.subject: ent:explicit-omit
requirements.canonical: The "explicit omit" rule IS applied recursively to the optional fields of the entity and to the subfields of its mandatory fields.
requirements.original: This applies recursively to the optional fields of the entity and to subfields of the mandatory fields.

requirements.subject: ent:implicit-omit
requirements.condition: variable or template variable with "implicit omit"
requirements.canonical: For a variable or template variable associated with an "implicit omit" optional attribute, the recursive procedure SHALL be applied after each assignment in the scope of its declaration, setting all optional fields without an assigned value definition to `omit`.
requirements.original: For variables and template variables associated with an "implicit omit" optional attribute, recursive procedure is applied to their optional fields after each assignment or usage as out or inout actual parameter in the scope of their declaration (e.g. after re-assigning parts or all of a variable's value) setting all optional fields that have no assigned value definition to omit.

requirements.subject: ent:implicit-omit
requirements.condition: variable or template variable with "implicit omit" used as out or inout actual parameter
requirements.canonical: For a variable or template variable associated with an "implicit omit" optional attribute, the recursive procedure SHALL be applied after each usage of it as an `out` or `inout` actual parameter in the scope of its declaration, setting all optional fields without an assigned value definition to `omit`.
requirements.original: For variables and template variables associated with an "implicit omit" optional attribute, recursive procedure is applied to their optional fields after each assignment or usage as out or inout actual parameter in the scope of their declaration (e.g. after re-assigning parts or all of a variable's value) setting all optional fields that have no assigned value definition to omit.

requirements.subject: ent:implicit-omit
requirements.canonical: Assigning the "implicit omit" attribute to a variable CAN have a negative runtime performance impact.
requirements.original: NOTE: Assigning the "implicit omit" attribute to a variable can have a negative runtime performance impact.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHOULD identify and optimize cases where the implicit omit operations are not needed, e.g. where it can be decided statically that no optional field could have become undefined.
requirements.original: Tool vendors are encouraged to identify and optimize particular cases where these operations are not needed (e.g. where it is possible to decide statically that no optional fields of the structure could have become undefined).

requirements.subject: ent:optional-attribute
requirements.canonical: An optional attribute SHALL NOT be associated directly with a data type definition, port type definition, procedure signature definition or import statement.
requirements.original: a) Data type, port type, procedure signature and import statements shall not have an optional attribute associated to them directly.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-attribute
requirements.condition: optional attribute associated with an enclosing definition
requirements.canonical: When an optional attribute is associated with a module, group, function, altstep, testcase, module control function or component type, it SHALL NOT have any effect on the data type, port type, procedure signature or import statement definitions contained in it.
requirements.original: When an optional attribute is associated to module, group, function, altstep, test case, control or component type containing such definitions, it shall not have any effect on the included data type, port type, procedure signature or import statement.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-attribute
requirements.canonical: At most one optional attribute SHALL be applied to each definition, each individual field reference or language element to which a with statement is associated.
requirements.original: b) At most one optional attribute shall be applied to each definition, each individual field reference or language element to which a with statement is associated.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute-retrieval-operation
requirements.canonical: TTCN-3 provides operations for retrieving the attribute values associated with a type, template, variable, constant or module parameter.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 provides a set of operations that can be used for retrieving attribute values associated with a type, template, variable, constant or module parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute-retrieval-operation
requirements.canonical: An attribute retrieval operation has the syntax ( Type | TemplateInstance ) "." ( `display` | `encode` | `variant` | `extension` | `optional` ) [ "(" Expression ")" ].
requirements.original:
( Type | TemplateInstance ) "." ( display | encode | variant | extension | optional )
  [ "(" Expression ")" ]

requirements.subject: ent:attribute-retrieval-operation
requirements.canonical: An attribute retrieval operation returns the actual value of the attribute associated with the type, template, variable, constant or module parameter preceding the dot.
requirements.original: The operation returns the actual value of an attribute associated with the type, template, variable, constant or module parameter that precedes the dot symbol.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute-retrieval-operation
requirements.canonical: The variable or template preceding the dot of an attribute retrieval operation MAY be uninitialized.
requirements.original: The value preceding the dot symbol may be unitialized.

ambiguity.issue: "value" is used for the entity preceding the dot, which is a type or template instance; "unitialized" is a misspelling of the glossary term "uninitialized".

improper_terms.proper: variable, constant, template or module parameter (TemplateInstance)

requirements.subject: ent:attribute-retrieval-operation
requirements.canonical: The attribute kind retrieved by an attribute retrieval operation IS denoted by the keyword (`display`, `encode`, `variant`, `extension` or `optional`) following the dot.
requirements.original: The attribute kind is denoted by the keyword following the dot symbol.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute-retrieval-operation
requirements.condition: display or optional attribute
requirements.canonical: An attribute retrieval operation for an attribute that can be present only once (`display`, `optional`) returns a value of universal charstring type.
requirements.original: The return value of the operations for retrieving attribute values is of a universal charstring type in case of attributes that can be present only once (display, optional) .

requirements.subject: ent:attribute-retrieval-operation
requirements.condition: display or optional attribute not defined
requirements.canonical: If a `display` or `optional` attribute is not defined, the attribute retrieval operation returns an empty string.
requirements.original: If such an attribute is not defined, the operation returns an empty string.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute-retrieval-operation
requirements.condition: encode, variant or extension attribute
requirements.canonical: An attribute retrieval operation for an attribute that can occur multiple times (`encode`, `variant`, `extension`) returns a value of a record of universal charstring type.
requirements.original: If the attribute can occur multiple times (encode, variant, extension), the operation returns a record of universal charstring type.

ambiguity.issue: It is not stated which "record of universal charstring" type is returned (no predefined type exists); the example assigns it to a user-defined type RUC. Chose: a value compatible with any record of universal charstring type.
readings: An attribute retrieval operation for `encode`, `variant` or `extension` returns a value compatible with any record of universal charstring type.
An attribute retrieval operation for `encode`, `variant` or `extension` returns a value of one specific (implicitly predefined) record of universal charstring type.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute-retrieval-operation
requirements.condition: encode, variant or extension attribute not present
requirements.canonical: If an `encode`, `variant` or `extension` attribute is not present, the attribute retrieval operation returns an empty record of value.
requirements.original: If such an attribute is not present, the operation returns an empty record of value.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute-retrieval-operation
requirements.canonical: An attribute retrieval operation for a `variant` attribute MAY be followed by an optional parameter.
requirements.original: The operation for getting a variant attribute value may be followed by an optional parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute-retrieval-operation
requirements.condition: no parameter
requirements.canonical: If no parameter is present, the `variant` attribute retrieval operation returns only the variants that are not bound to any particular encoding.
requirements.original: If no parameter is present, the operation returns only variants that are not bound to any particular encoding.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute-retrieval-operation
requirements.condition: parameter present
requirements.canonical: If the parameter is present, the `variant` attribute retrieval operation returns the variants that are bound to the encoding referenced by the parameter.
requirements.original: If the parameter is present, the returned value will contain variants that are bound to the encoding referenced by the parameter.

ambiguity.issue: "will contain variants that are bound to the encoding" does not say whether variants not bound to any encoding are also included. Chose: only the bound variants.
readings: If the parameter is present, the `variant` attribute retrieval operation returns only the variants bound to the referenced encoding.
If the parameter is present, the `variant` attribute retrieval operation returns the variants bound to the referenced encoding plus the variants not bound to any encoding.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute-retrieval-operation
requirements.canonical: The optional parameter of an attribute retrieval operation SHALL be used only for retrieving `variant` attributes.
requirements.original: a) The optional parameter of the operation shall be used only for getting variant attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute-retrieval-operation
requirements.canonical: The Expression in the optional parameter of an attribute retrieval operation SHALL be of universal charstring type.
requirements.original: b) The Expression in optional parameter of the operation shall be of the universal charstring type.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute-retrieval-operation
requirements.condition: parameter value is not a valid encode attribute
requirements.canonical: An error SHALL be produced if the Expression in the optional parameter of an attribute retrieval operation is not one of the valid encode attributes of the referenced type or template.
requirements.original: c) An error shall be produced if the Expression in the optional parameters is not one of the valid encode attributes.

ambiguity.issue: It is not stated whether the error is a compile-time error (when the Expression is constant) or a runtime error, nor whose encode attributes are meant. Chose: the encode attributes of the entity preceding the dot, checked whenever the value is known.
readings: A compile-time error SHALL be produced if the constant Expression is not one of the encode attributes of the entity preceding the dot.
A runtime error SHALL be produced when the evaluated Expression is not one of the encode attributes of the entity preceding the dot.

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.canonical: The `setencode` operation CAN be used on a port or set of ports to dynamically select, for the affected ports, a single encode attribute value for a type that has multiple encode attributes.
requirements.original: The setencode operation can be used on a port or set of ports to dynamically select for the affected ports a single encode attribute value to be used for a type that has multiple encode attributes attached to it.

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.canonical: The `setencode` operation has the syntax ( SingleExpression | `all port` | `self` ) "." `setencode` "(" Type "," SingleExpression ")".
requirements.original: (SingleExpression | ( all port ) | self ) "." setencode"(" Type "," SingleExpression ")"

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.canonical: The `setencode` operation dynamically restricts the encode attribute values of the referenced type, or of its fields or elements, to a single value.
requirements.original: The setencode operation dynamically restricts the number of encode attribute values of a referenced type or its fields or elements to a single value.

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.condition: single port reference precedes the dot
requirements.canonical: When the `setencode` operation is applied to a single port reference, the encoding configuration IS valid for all sending and receiving operations of that port.
requirements.original: Dependent on the language element preceding the dot, the encoding configuration is valid either for all sending and receiving operations of a single port (single port reference), sending and receiving operations of all ports of the current component (all `port notation) or for all codec functions and communication operations of` the current component (self keyword).

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.condition: `all port` precedes the dot
requirements.canonical: When the `setencode` operation is applied with `all port`, the encoding configuration IS valid for the sending and receiving operations of all ports of the current component.
requirements.original: Dependent on the language element preceding the dot, the encoding configuration is valid either for all sending and receiving operations of a single port (single port reference), sending and receiving operations of all ports of the current component (all `port notation) or for all codec functions and communication operations of` the current component (self keyword).

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.condition: `self` precedes the dot
requirements.canonical: When the `setencode` operation is applied with `self`, the encoding configuration IS valid for all codec functions and communication operations of the current component.
requirements.original: Dependent on the language element preceding the dot, the encoding configuration is valid either for all sending and receiving operations of a single port (single port reference), sending and receiving operations of all ports of the current component (all `port notation) or for all codec functions and communication operations of` the current component (self keyword).

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.condition: type has multiple encode attributes and expression equals one of them
requirements.canonical: If the referenced type contains multiple encode attributes and the expression of the `setencode` operation equals one of them, the `setencode` operation reduces the list of encode attributes to the selected one.
requirements.original: If the referenced type contains multiple encode attributes and the expression provided in the setencode operation is equal to one of these encode attribute values, the statement reduces the list of encode attributes to the selected one.

ambiguity.issue: The behaviour when the expression matches none of the encode attributes (or the type has only one) is not specified. Chose: the stated case only.
readings: If the expression matches none of the encode attributes, the `setencode` operation has no effect.
If the expression matches none of the encode attributes, the `setencode` operation causes an error.

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.canonical: The `setencode` reduction procedure IS applied recursively to all elements and fields of the referenced type.
requirements.original: The procedure is applied recursively to all elements and fields or the referenced type.

ambiguity.issue: "fields or the referenced type" is a typo for "fields of the referenced type".

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.canonical: After the `setencode` operation is executed, all other encode attributes of the referenced type and the variants related to them IS dynamically disabled and invisible to the codec.
requirements.original: After executing the operation, all other encode attributes and variants related to them are dynamically disabled and invisible to the codec.

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.canonical: A repeated call of the `setencode` operation always uses the static attributes that are valid for the referenced type.
requirements.original: Repeated call of the setencode operation always uses the static attributes that are valid for the referenced type.

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.canonical: Previous calls of the `setencode` operation referencing the same type IS NOT considered by a repeated call.
requirements.original: Previous calls of the setencode operation referencing the type are not considered in this case.

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.canonical: The encoding of a type CAN be changed during test execution by repeated `setencode` calls using different encodings.
requirements.original: This way it is possible to change the encoding during test execution using different encodings.

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.canonical: The `setencode` operation MAY reference a field or element of a type using an extended type reference.
requirements.original: It is allowed to reference a field or element of a type using an extended type reference in the setencode operation.

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.canonical: A `setencode` operation with an extended type reference IS useful for payload fields of container protocols and allows dynamic configuration of the proper encoding for payload fields.
requirements.original: This operation is useful for payload fields of container protocols and allows dynamic configuration of the proper encoding for payload fields.

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.condition: an extended type reference was used in an earlier setencode call
requirements.canonical: If an extended type reference was used in a `setencode` operation, subsequent `setencode` calls for the whole type or any element containing the referenced field SHALL NOT change the encoding dynamically configured for that field or element and its sub-fields.
requirements.original: If the extended type reference is used, following calls of the setencode operation for the whole type or any element that contains the referenced payload field won't change the encoding that was dynamically configured for this field or element (and its sub-fields).

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.condition: setencode applied to a single port
requirements.canonical: If the `setencode` operation is applied to a single port, the referenced type SHALL be listed in the in or out type list of the related port type, or be a reference to a field or element, on any level of nesting, of such a type.
requirements.original: a) If the setencode operation is applied to a single port, the referenced type shall be either listed in the in or out type list of the related port type or it shall be a reference to a field or element on any level of nesting of a type listed in the in or out type list of the related port type.

ambiguity.issue: The port type lists are "in", "out" and "inout"; the restriction mentions only "in or out". The example uses an inout list. Chose: types in in, out or inout lists are allowed.
readings: If `setencode` is applied to a single port, the referenced type SHALL be listed in the in, out or inout list of the port type (or be a nested field of such a type).
If `setencode` is applied to a single port, the referenced type SHALL be listed in the in or out list of the port type only (or be a nested field of such a type).

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.canonical: The SingleExpression in the second parameter of the `setencode` operation SHALL be compatible with the universal charstring type.
requirements.original: b) The SingleExpression used in the second parameter of the setencode operation shall be compatible with the universal charstring type.

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.condition: a SingleExpression precedes the dot
requirements.canonical: If present, the SingleExpression preceding the `setencode` keyword SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: c) If present, the SingleExpression preceding the setencode keyword shall be of a port type.
